info.title: Hyperdash Data API
info.description: Hyperliquid data from Hyperdash's own nodes and stored datasets; requests never call Hyperliquid's public API. Every response reports the credits it cost.

get.description:
Ascending candles in [start_time, end_time). 1m: range ≤ 7 days. Sub-minute (1s, 15s, 30s): the last ~23 hours only, buckets with trades only, range ≤ 1 day. Coarser intervals: range ≤ 7 days (< 1h bars), 30 days (< 1d) or 365 days (1d and coarser); ≤ 5,000 bars per page (meta.forming flags an unfinished last bar). Page with the cursor. HIP-4 outcome markets: coin = #<outcome id><side> (e.g. #232960). Trades follow Hyperliquid's candles: spot borrow liquidations by the backstop (off-book at 0.99 × mark) and internal vault netting are not trades; trades with a liquidated party count in `v` and `n` but set prices only in a bar that has nothing else (`liq_only`); open and close are the first and last trade: in execution order where bars come from Hyperdash's node archive (the live window, and intervals other than 1m within the archive); bars from the durable 1m store (1m older than about 30 minutes, coarser intervals older than the archive) order trades inside one millisecond by taker order and sweep position, which matches the execution order on all but about 0.05 % of bar edges.

Pricing: base + per row; ×2 above 24 h. Scope: `markets:read`.

parameters.name: coin
parameters.description: Market, e.g. BTC, xyz:TSLA, #232960 (an outcome side; URL-encode # as %23).

parameters.name: interval
parameters.description: 1m (exact archive, ≤ 7 days per call), 1s / 15s / 30s (last ~23 h, ≤ 1 day per call) or 3m, 5m, 15m, 30m, 1h, 2h, 4h, 8h, 12h, 1d, 3d, 1w, 1M (range ≤ 7 / 30 / 365 days by bar size).

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Rows per page.

parameters.name: start_time
parameters.description: Start, epoch ms (inclusive). Default: end_time − 24 h.

parameters.name: end_time
parameters.description: End, epoch ms. Default: now.

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: Opaque cursor from next_cursor (replaces the range).

parameters.name: X-Max-Credits
parameters.description: Refuse (free) if the request could cost more. The check compares your limit with the MOST the request could cost, before it runs: GET /v1/quote with the same route and parameters (cursor included) returns exactly that maximum, never below the charge. Where the number of rows cannot be known from the request (a wallet's or the exchange's current state, every market, price levels per bar…) that maximum is priced at the route's row cap (plus any range tier or node reads), while you are charged for the rows actually returned: such operations say so in their pricing note. There, omit X-Max-Credits or set it to at least the quoted ceiling.

get.description:
Ascending by (time, coin, tid) in [start_time, end_time]: every raw fill (each match with each resting order is its own row). `aggregate=true`: ascending by (time, order id), one fill per order per block as hyperdash.com shows them (Hyperliquid's aggregateByTime: an order's partial fills in one block merged — size, fee, builder fee, deployer fee, priority gas and closed PnL summed, size-weighted price, the first fill's tid, start position and direction), read from Hyperdash's node fill store, so counts are lower than raw. Range ≤ 7 days; page with the cursor.

Pricing: base + per row; ×2 above 24 h. Scope: `accounts:read`.

get.description:
Live clearinghouse state for one dex: the core exchange by default, or a HIP-3 builder dex via `dex`. One dex per call. meta.margin: the dex's margin summary (account value, notional, raw USD, margin used, withdrawable) and its cross-margin part. Rows also carry `leverage` {type, value} and `cum_funding` {all_time, since_open, since_change} as nested objects (the original shape), with the same values as the flat fields.

Pricing: base + per position + one node read. X-Max-Credits / GET /v1/quote: this route's ceiling is priced at its cap of 500 rows, whatever the parameters (this route reserves the same rows for any request, mostly because their number cannot be known before it runs), plus any range tier or node reads; you are charged for the rows returned. Use GET /v1/quote for the exact ceiling, and omit X-Max-Credits or set it to at least that ceiling. Scope: `accounts:read`.

get.description:
All perp markets of one dex (core exchange by default) with live prices, funding, open interest and volume. HIP-3 dexes are computed by Hyperdash from its own nodes: `mark_px` there is Hyperdash's estimate (`mark_px_estimated`; usually within 0.05 % of the exchange's mark, but it can stay at the oracle and differ by about 1 % on a market trading away from it) and the predicted `funding` is null until Hyperdash's computation is verified against the exchange's samples (`funding_unverified`; `last_settled_funding` carries the rate settled at the last hour).

Pricing: base + two node reads. X-Max-Credits / GET /v1/quote: this route's ceiling is priced at its cap of 1,000 rows, whatever the parameters (this route reserves the same rows for any request, mostly because their number cannot be known before it runs), plus any range tier or node reads; you are charged for the rows returned. Use GET /v1/quote for the exact ceiling, and omit X-Max-Credits or set it to at least that ceiling. Scope: `markets:read`.

parameters.description: Refuse (free) if the request could cost more. collateral_token.description: Collateral token of the dex (spot token index; 0 = USDC)

get.description:
Every running (or trigger-waiting) TWAP order of one core-exchange perp from the latest node state snapshot: wallet, side, total / executed / remaining size, executed notional, progress, duration, next slice. Largest first; at most 100 per answer (and your plan's wallet-list cap). meta.snapshot_id identifies the node state. The snapshot is cut from the node state every 10,000 blocks (~12 min) and published ~3 min later, so it is 3 to 15 min old: its block time is in meta (snapshot_time, epoch ms; snapshot_time_estimated = true when derived from its TWAPs' next slices, within 15 s; null when unknown — no running TWAP to date it by). TWAPs started, ended or terminated since are not reflected.

Pricing: base + per row. X-Max-Credits / GET /v1/quote: this route's ceiling is priced at its cap of 100 rows, whatever the parameters (this route reserves the same rows for any request, mostly because their number cannot be known before it runs), plus any range tier or node reads; you are charged for the rows returned. Use GET /v1/quote for the exact ceiling, and omit X-Max-Credits or set it to at least that ceiling. Scope: `analytics:read`.

get.summary: TWAP stop and trigger levels of one market
get.description:
Where running TWAP flow switches off and waiting TWAP flow switches on, from the latest node state snapshot (meta.snapshot_id): one row per price level, kind and side. kind=stop: running TWAPs that stop once the price reaches px (a buy from below, a sell from above; HL announced it will pause them there instead and resume when the price comes back). kind=trigger: TWAPs waiting to start once the price moves above / below px (a waiting TWAP's stop applies once it has started). Each row sums the TWAPs' remaining size and their average size per minute (remaining size over the remaining scheduled time, both at the snapshot's cut — meta.as_of = meta.snapshot_time, null when unknown; a running TWAP of an undated snapshot counts its time left in its own 30 s slices —; a waiting TWAP: its size over its duration). The snapshot is cut from the node state every 10,000 blocks (~12 min) and published ~3 min later, so it is 3 to 15 min old: its block time is in meta (snapshot_time, epoch ms; snapshot_time_estimated = true when derived from its TWAPs' next slices, within 15 s; null when unknown — no running TWAP to date it by). TWAPs started, ended or terminated since are not reflected. Aggregated, no wallets. Highest price first; meta.levels counts every level and meta.truncated is true when more than 500 exist. meta adds the market's unconditional TWAP flow: running buy / sell TWAPs, their remaining size and average size per minute, and how many wait for a trigger.

Pricing: base + per row. X-Max-Credits / GET /v1/quote: this route's ceiling is priced at its cap of 500 rows, whatever the parameters (this route reserves the same rows for any request, mostly because their number cannot be known before it runs), plus any range tier or node reads; you are charged for the rows returned. Use GET /v1/quote for the exact ceiling, and omit X-Max-Credits or set it to at least that ceiling. Scope: `analytics:read`.

get.description:
Hyperdash's own margin engine, recomputed every sweep: per position the notional, mark and maintenance-margin requirement at its tier rate, grouped by margin book (cross per dex, or isolated); meta: equity and maintenance margin per book, margin mode, collateral and the sweep time. Covers accounts with at least $100k equity or gross notional; smaller accounts return no rows. Also the BTC move that liquidates the account (hyperdash.com's account-risk view): every coin projected through its 30 / 60 / 90-day hourly beta to BTC (per row: beta, correlation, beta_fallback = no usable history, projected 1:1), positions and margin tiers held constant; meta.btc_move = the closest cross book's move (signed fraction: −0.12 = BTC down 12 %; null = no plausible move within −95 % … +300 %), meta.btc_liquidation_px, per book btc_move / btc_delta; an isolated row's own move to its engine liquidation price (btc_move). A statistical projection from engine-exact inputs, not an engine-exact liquidation price. When the betas can't be loaded (or the positions server lacks the projection inputs), the margin rows are still served with the BTC fields null and meta.btc_projection false.

Pricing: base. X-Max-Credits / GET /v1/quote: this route's ceiling is priced at its cap of 1,000 rows, whatever the parameters (this route reserves the same rows for any request, mostly because their number cannot be known before it runs), plus any range tier or node reads; you are charged for the rows returned. Use GET /v1/quote for the exact ceiling, and omit X-Max-Credits or set it to at least that ceiling. Scope: `accounts:read`.

get.summary: Position-action footprint (open / close × long / short × taker / maker per price row)
get.description:
Per bar and price row, the size and notional of every fill leg split by what it did to the trader's position: open long, close long, open short, close short, each as taker or maker. Both legs of every trade count (they are different wallets' actions), so the totals are twice the market volume by design. A flip (long > short or short > long) splits exactly at the position it closed. Only whole bars inside the window that ended at least 2 minutes ago are served (best effort: late fills within that delay can still land); an empty window returns no rows. row_size: 'auto' (default: a band from the window's first price) or a decimal at least the auto size / 10. ≤ 2,500 rows per page (a page ends on a whole bar; one bar above it: use a coarser row_size or interval). A page reads ≤ 4 h at 1m and ≤ 1 day otherwise; the cursor continues.

Pricing: base + per row; ×2 for a page over 4 h. X-Max-Credits / GET /v1/quote: this route's ceiling is priced at its cap of 2,500 rows, whatever the parameters (this route reserves the same rows for any request, mostly because their number cannot be known before it runs), plus any range tier or node reads; you are charged for the rows returned. get.description:
A wallet's cumulative PnL over a window, like hyperdash.com's profile chart, computed by Hyperdash from its own data: the hourly account-value snapshots (as GET /v1/accounts/{address}/account-value) and the capital moved in or out of that value, with GET /v1/accounts/{address}/pnl-calendar's definition (deposits, withdrawals, transfers with other wallets on any side at their USD value, vaults, borrow / lend and HYPE staking transfers from 2026-09-23; before it the perp-cash USDC moves). Per bucket: the account value at its last point (defined next), the net flows assigned to its points, and pnl = account value − the value at the window start − net flows since. A snapshot with a ledger entry of the wallet (any transfer, including its own spot↔perp moves) in the 20 minutes before it is not a point, because the stored value takes transfers in up to about 20 minutes late — except each UTC day's close as the calendar picks it (its last snapshot, or the one before it), which is always a point. Each capital move counts at the first point at or after it, and the value at the start is the last point-eligible snapshot before the window on the day of the last snapshot before it or the day before (if neither day has one, that last snapshot itself; 0 if there is none). Account value change minus flows only: no realized / unrealized split; for a unified account it is the whole collateral pool's PnL, as in the calendar, and the calendar's known limits apply. A one-time step from a change in how Hyperdash computes the stored value (2026-11: flat classic accounts' spot wallets) is in net_flows, not in pnl, with the calendar's exceptions (wallets active around the switch, portfolio-margin accounts). Between two daily closes, pnl changes by the sum of GET /v1/accounts/{address}/pnl-calendar's daily PnL over those days. `window` sets the bucket and default range: day (15 min buckets, last 24 h; with start_time ≤ 7 days), week (1 h, last 7 days; ≤ 30 days), month (4 h, last 30 days; ≤ 90 days), alltime (1 day, from 2025-08-25 — the first snapshots — through the whole history, buckets widened to whole multi-day buckets past 1,000 days; with start_time ≤ 365 days). Buckets without a point are absent. One page.

Pricing: base × range tier (≤7 d ×1, ≤30 d ×3, ≤90 d ×4, ≤365 d ×10, longer ×11). X-Max-Credits / GET /v1/quote: this route's ceiling is priced at its cap of 1,000 rows, whatever the parameters (this route reserves the same rows for any request, mostly because their number cannot be known before it runs), plus any range tier or node reads; you are charged for the rows returned. Use GET /v1/quote for the exact ceiling, and omit X-Max-Credits or set it to at least that ceiling. Scope: `accounts:read`.

get.description:
Accounts ranked by how close a BTC move takes them to liquidation (or by equity, notional, leverage): the BTC move (signed fraction: −0.12 = BTC down 12 %) and BTC price that liquidate the account's closest cross book, its equity, notionals, cross leverage, BTC-equivalent exposure, maintenance and cushion. Hyperdash's margin engine (every sweep, from our nodes) gives each account's exact margin inputs; every coin is then projected through its 30 / 60 / 90-day hourly beta to BTC (coins without usable history at 1.0), positions and margin tiers held constant: a statistical projection, not an engine-exact liquidation price. A book liquidates at equity = maintenance (portfolio margin: maintenance = 0.95 × the liquidation value). No plausible move (outside −95 % … +300 %) = null. Covers accounts with ≥ $100k equity or gross notional (the engine's export). One page (the top `limit`); meta: btc_mark, computed_at (sweep), input_at (the older of the newest node event and oracle update), stale (input older than 60 s), the matching account count.

Pricing: base + per row. Scope: `analytics:read`.

get.description:
The same accounts as GET /v1/accounts/liquidation-risk, bucketed by the BTC move that liquidates them: per 1 % bucket from −50 % to +50 % (floor of the move), the accounts, their cross notional and equity, and the BTC price at the bucket's lower bound. Accounts without a plausible move, or outside ±50 %, are counted in meta (unplaced); accounts whose margin is not certified yet (positions opened since the engine's last state snapshot, ~12 min, or a pool, not portfolio margin, that a fill since then left below its maintenance requirement) are left out and counted in meta (uncertain; null when the positions server does not report certification, and then no account is left out). Hyperdash's margin engine (every sweep, from our nodes) gives each account's exact margin inputs; every coin is then projected through its 30 / 60 / 90-day hourly beta to BTC (coins without usable history at 1.0), positions and margin tiers held constant: a statistical projection, not an engine-exact liquidation price. A book liquidates at equity = maintenance (portfolio margin: maintenance = 0.95 × the liquidation value). No plausible move (outside −95 % … +300 %) = null. Covers accounts with ≥ $100k equity or gross notional (the engine's export). meta: btc_mark, computed_at (sweep), input_at (the older of the newest node event and oracle update), stale (input older than 60 s), the matching account count. No wallets.

Pricing: base. X-Max-Credits / GET /v1/quote: this route's ceiling is priced at its cap of 100 rows, whatever the parameters (this route reserves the same rows for any request, mostly because their number cannot be known before it runs), plus any range tier or node reads; you are charged for the rows returned. Use GET /v1/quote for the exact ceiling, and omit X-Max-Credits or set it to at least that ceiling. Scope: `analytics:read`.

Cohort = account value at that day's close: small < $10K, medium $10K–100K, large $100K–1M, whale $1M–5M, apex $5M+, unknown (no close snapshot yet, or none); all = every trader. get.summary: Completed trades of one wallet: whole history, filters and sorts (hyperdash.com's Completed Trades tab)
get.description:
Every round trip (a position opened and fully closed) from hyperdash.com's completed-trades table, the source of the site's Completed Trades and Best Trades tabs and of GET /v1/accounts/{address}/stats: whole history, filtered by market, side, result and minimum notional (|size| × entry price), sorted by any of the site's columns (default: newest close first). `limit` trades per page; page with the cursor — pages start at offsets ≤ 10,000 (as the site), so one query reaches at most 10,000 + limit trades (meta.truncated = more exist: narrow with a filter or reverse the order). Pages are offsets into the live table, as on the site: trades that close while you page shift newest-first pages (a trade can repeat); order=asc walks stably. meta.total: matching trades when a filter is set, counted within your plan's history window on the first page and carried by the cursor (null without filters). Coverage: wallets Hyperdash has admitted to that table (every wallet trading since ~August 2025 and any wallet viewed on hyperdash.com; an older inactive wallet can have no rows), trades from the fills archive (2025-03). Your plan's history window applies (meta.history_from): trades closed before it are not delivered, counted or paged through, in every sort and order. The first page pins the window for the query's cursor so offsets stay stable while it slides; a later page leaves out trades that have since aged out of it. A cursor continues for up to a day past its window; after that, or once your plan's history is shorter than when the query started, it is refused with history_limit: restart the query. Same round trips as GET /v1/accounts/{address}/trades, which pages a close-time range (≤ 90 days, ascending) from the node trade store instead. net_pnl = gross − signed fees (maker rebates add) + funding; fees = Σ |fee| (as /stats).

get.description:
Daily PnL like the hyperdash.com PnL calendar, per UTC day from `from` to `to` (at most 366 dates, as the site): the change in the wallet's account value (GET /v1/accounts/{address}/account-value) from the previous close to the day's close minus the capital moved in or out in between. A day's close is its last snapshot (about 23:00 UTC); when that snapshot has a ledger entry of the wallet (any transfer, including its own spot↔perp moves) in the 20 minutes before it and the snapshot before it (about 22:00) has none, the close is that earlier snapshot: the stored value takes transfers in up to about 20 minutes late, so a move just before the close is counted the next day instead, and that as a % of the previous close. The account value is the equity on every perp dex plus the spot wallet for a classic account (with or without an open position), or for unified and portfolio-margin accounts their pooled collateral; it never includes lent tokens, staked HYPE or vault equity. For a unified account (spot and perps share one collateral pool) PnL is the change of that whole pool — available spot USDC, perp equity and its other tokens at their price — minus the capital moved in or out: its moves between spot and perp are internal, and supplying to lending or staking HYPE takes value out. Capital moved: deposits and withdrawals, transfers with other wallets on any side (spot, perp or HIP-3 dex, at their USD value), vault deposits and withdrawals, borrow / lend (supplying or repaying takes value out, withdrawing or borrowing brings it in) and HYPE staking transfers; moves between the wallet's own spot and perp balances are not. Stablecoins count at face value, HYPE and UBTC at the HYPE / BTC perp's close of the last whole minute before the move. Before 2026-09-23 the stored account value is perp equity only and the capital moves are the perp-cash ones (USDC deposits, withdrawals, transfers, spot↔perp); days before 2025-08-25 come from the wallet's fills. When Hyperdash changes how the stored value is computed (2026-11: a classic account with no open position now counts its spot wallet, as a positioned one already did), the one-time step is booked as capital moved, not PnL — except for a wallet that traded or moved capital within about an hour of the switch, and for portfolio-margin accounts (their valuation changed at the same time), whose switch day can carry part of the step. Known limits: from 2026-09-23 until that change, a classic account with no open position was stored without its spot wallet, so on those days its spot-side transfers show as PnL (those stored values cannot be rebuilt); lending interest and staking rewards are not counted as PnL (they arrive with the moves); protocol and treasury wallets (their spot is token supply, left out of their value) do not match their transfers; a unified account emptied to zero keeps its last stored value until it holds funds again; when both of a day's last two snapshots follow a ledger entry by under 20 minutes, the close stays the last one and can miss that move until the next day; idle collateral on a HIP-3 dex without a position is not counted.

Pricing: base + per row. X-Max-Credits / GET /v1/quote: this route's ceiling is priced at its cap of 400 rows, whatever the parameters (this route reserves the same rows for any request, mostly because their number cannot be known before it runs), plus any range tier or node reads; you are charged for the rows returned. Use GET /v1/quote for the exact ceiling, and omit X-Max-Credits or set it to at least that ceiling. Scope: `analytics:read`.

get.description:
A wallet's cumulative realized perp PnL over a window: the realized line (rPnL) of hyperdash.com's profile PnL chart, computed by Hyperdash from its own fills and funding. Realized = closed PnL − fees (every fee token at face value; rebates add) + funding; spot and outcome fills are excluded. Funding before 2025-09-27 10:00 UTC comes from each completed trade's funding, booked at its close (a trade open across that instant has the part before it booked at 09:59:59.999). Rows: start_time, then the running total at the end of each `interval` bucket with activity that ends before end_time (buckets count from start_time; pass a UTC-aligned start_time for UTC hours / days), then end_time. The series starts at 0, or with `anchor=true` on the wallet's All Time leaderboard realized PnL (the board's value at its last refresh minus what the series adds between start_time and then); `anchored` says whether that applied (the wallet has a board row with a realized split, and start_time is not after the board's refresh). Known limit: a self-matched fill counts one leg, except on the full UTC days the daily table serves (below) from 2025-07-28, where it counts both legs. `interval` sets the bucket and the range: 5m (default the last day, ≤ 7 days), 1h (default 7 days, ≤ 90 days), 1d (default 90 days, ≤ 365 days). 1d whose window is longer than 90 days, or with `anchor=true` whose start_time is more than 90 days and 10 minutes before now, reads Hyperdash's certified daily table: buckets are UTC days (points at the UTC midnight after each active day), and while a day the range needs is being rebuilt the call answers 503 `unavailable` (retry later, or read ≤ 90 days). `anchor=true` reads every fill from start_time up to now (whatever end_time), so start_time must then be within that bound of now, and the range that counts for this call is start_time → now, not start_time → end_time. One page.

Pricing: base × range tier (≤1 d ×1, ≤7 d ×3, ≤30 d ×10, ≤90 d ×25, ≤365 d ×25 with interval 1d); with anchor=true the range is start_time → now whatever end_time (the anchor reads every fill up to now; quote with range_ms = now − start_time); a range containing 2025-09-27 09:59:59.999 UTC (the funding-source correction, which reads the trades open across it) is priced as at least 30 days. Scope: `analytics:read`.

get.summary: IOC fills that paid priority gas

Growth plans and above.

One query returns at most your plan's wallet-list cap across its pages (Growth 500, Scale and Enterprise 1,000); a query cut there ends with meta.truncated = true and no next_cursor: start a new one from the last row's time (its block is served again from the start; a block larger than the cap itself is cut there: start after its time to go on). meta.start_time / meta.end_time = the window this page covers: rows are complete in it outside meta.gaps ([{from, to}] not proven, e.g. a worker restart). meta.live_to = the live feed's newest block time (meta.as_of), meta.stale = true when it lags > 15 s. Growth plans and above.

Pricing: base + per row. Scope: `analytics:read`.
